title: Course Overview and Control Fundamentals
focus: Course structure, basic control concepts, inverted pendulum motivation, block diagrams, input/output/state, and open-loop versus closed-loop control.
topics: What control engineering studies and why it matters
Inverted pendulum as a classical benchmark
Input, output, state, open-loop control, closed-loop control, and feedback

title: Linear Dynamical Systems and Transfer Functions
focus: Linear dynamical systems, nonlinear-to-linear modeling, Laplace transform, and transfer-function representation.
topics: Linear system concepts and modeling assumptions
From nonlinear CartPole dynamics to a linear model
lab: Modeling practice based on linearized control examples.

title: Closed-Loop Stability and Root Locus
focus: Closed-loop transfer functions, characteristic equations, poles and zeros, stability, Routh criterion, and root-locus analysis.

title: Frequency Response, State Space, and RL Introduction
focus: Frequency-response analysis, Bode and Nyquist plots, margins, state-space perspective, controllability, observability, and a first RL introduction.
topics: Frequency response, Bode plot, and Nyquist plot
Controllability, observability, state feedback, and RL motivation

title: CartPole, Reinforcement Learning, and DQN Practice
focus: Reinforcement learning overview, Q-learning, DQN, replay buffer, target network, and a practical CartPole workflow.
topics: Deep Q-Network with replay buffer and target network
Torch, Gymnasium, Stable-Baselines3, and practical setup
lab: CartPole DQN practice and environment setup.

title: RIP Modeling, Hardware System Introduction, and STM32 Setup
focus: Rotary inverted pendulum modeling, hardware architecture, sensors, motor driver, STM32 development setup, and experimental-platform overview.
topics: Rotary inverted pendulum hardware and coordinate definitions
Potentiometer, encoder, DC motor, and TB6612FNG driver
Modeling path from physical system to control-oriented representation
lab: Hardware platform introduction and STM32 environment setup.

title: Hardware Assembly, Sensor Test, and Bellman-to-Control Bridge
focus: Physical wiring, sensor and motor tests, angle logging, and the conceptual bridge from Bellman optimality to HJB, LQR, MPC, and RL.
topics: Sensor calibration and motor actuation checks
Bellman principle, HJB equation, LQR, MPC, and RL connections
lab: Run sensor and motor test programs and collect calibrated logs.

title: Optimal Control Experiments on the Rotary Inverted Pendulum
focus: Sampled-data modeling, velocity estimation, LQR and MPC design, embedded implementation, and hardware experiment comparison.
topics: LQR gain computation and STM32 implementation
MPC prediction, cost function, constraints, and hardware testing
lab: Run and compare LQR and MPC hardware experiments.

title: State Observers for Control of the Rotary Inverted Pendulum
focus: Observer design for RIP control using Luenberger and Kalman observers with observer-based LQR/MPC experiments.
topics: Measured outputs and unmeasured state reconstruction
Luenberger observer poles and error dynamics
Steady-state Kalman observer and noise tuning
lab: Compare direct velocity estimation with observer-estimated states.

title: Simulation Training of DQN, PPO, and TD3 for the Rotary Inverted Pendulum
focus: Gymnasium-style RIP simulation, training workflows, and policy export for DQN, PPO, and TD3.
topics: Policy evaluation and export for deployment
lab: Train and evaluate reinforcement learning controllers in simulation.

title: Sim-to-Real Deployment of Reinforcement Learning Controllers
focus: Export trained policies, deploy DQN/PPO/TD3 controllers to embedded hardware, and log physical-system responses.
topics: DQN, PPO, and TD3 deployment programs
lab: Deploy trained RL controllers and record physical experiment data.

title: Hybrid Control, Sim-to-Real Improvement, and Final Demonstration
focus: Hybrid control ideas, sim-to-real improvement strategies, delay issues, and final demonstration organization.
topics: Sim-to-real improvement and residual adaptation ideas
lab: Prepare final comparison, demonstration, and report materials.
